newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-West power moves lower on lackluster demand.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-West power moves lower on lackluster demand.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West moved lower Friday amid lacklustre shoulder month demand, industry sources said.
"September is the worst month for scheduling electricity," said one marketer, adding "it's a very slow usage month."

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), on peak electricity for a 16-hour block for delivery Saturday was talked near $11.00, while Sunday was discussed near $10.50, the brokers and marketers said.
Monday on-peak power was assessed in the $13.00-15.00 range, from next day prices on Thursday of $15.00-17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the sources said.
Off-peak power was pegged in the $7.50-8.00 range from next-day discussion at $8.00-$8.50 on Thursday.

On-peak prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for weekend delivery were said to be discussed in the $14.00-15.00 per MWh range, with Monday power also near those levels from next-day discussion at $15.50-17.50 on Thursday, the sources said.
Off-peak power was said to be in the $8.00-9.00 range from near $11.00 in Thursday talk, the sources said.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for weekend delivery were quoted steady in the $14.00-16.00 range for Monday, the sources said.
Longer-term ECAR peak power prices also held steady, with the remainder of September discussed near $15.50 and October at close to $17.00.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for weekend delivery in the north area was assessed steady in the $13.00-14.00 range, while on-peak power in the south was said to be steady in the 16.00-16.50 range, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
